candidates.label: AHU economizer / discharge air temperature fault
candidates.detail: The air handler's economizer damper is stuck, mis-staged or its outdoor-air lockout is wrong, or the discharge air setpoint is too warm, so supply air is not cold enough for cooling even though fan, static and box airflow are all fine.

check.name: ahu_discharge_temp
check.text: In the control system or at the air handler, read supply (discharge) air temperature, its setpoint, mixed-air temperature and economizer damper position against outdoor air. Abnormal if discharge air is more than about 3 F above setpoint or above roughly 58 F during a cooling call, or the economizer position does not match the outdoor conditions.

candidates.label: Supply air temperature reset or chilled-water failure
candidates.detail: Central cooling is not delivering cold air: chilled-water valve stuck or failed, DX stage locked out, or discharge air temperature reset has raised the setpoint, so boxes deliver full airflow but air is too warm.

check.name: ahu_coil_check
check.text: At the air handler, compare cooling coil entering and leaving air temperature (or chilled-water valve command versus position and water delta-T). Abnormal if the temperature drop across the coil is small while the valve or stage is commanded on.

candidates.label: Reheat valve leaking by or overheating the room
candidates.detail: Hot water passes through a reheat valve that should be closed (or an electric stage sticks on), so the room is warm even with full cooling airflow; the technician sees good airflow but the wrong temperature.

check.name: reheat_off_downstream_temp
check.text: With the box commanded to full cooling and reheat commanded closed or off, measure supply air temperature just downstream of the reheat coil and compare with the inlet air temperature, and feel the pipes. Abnormal if the air is warmed by more than about 3 F, or the coil piping is hot.

candidates.label: Wrong operating mode: heating sequence active or ahu in warm-up/changeover
candidates.detail: The box or whole air handler is in a heating, warm-up or seasonal changeover mode (or the central system is on a heating/cooling changeover schedule), so warm air is being supplied and the box limits airflow to heating maximum.

check.name: ahu_mode_changeover
check.text: In the control system, read the air handler's operating mode, system heating/cooling changeover state, and discharge temperature setpoint against the season and the box's cooling/heating mode flag. Abnormal if the central mode or box mode disagrees with what the zone needs.

candidates.label: Return/exhaust or room pressure imbalance
candidates.detail: Return path is blocked (closed fire/transfer damper, undercut door, blocked return grille) or exhaust fans overpower the zone, so supply air cannot enter the room and airflow or comfort is poor even with a healthy box.

check.name: room_pressure_door
check.text: In the room, close the door and check door pressure: watch whether the door is hard to open or whistles, measure room-to-corridor differential pressure with a manometer, and inspect the return grille or transfer path. Abnormal if the differential exceeds about 0.02 in. w.c. or the return path is blocked.

candidates.label: Fire/smoke or isolation damper partly closed in the duct
candidates.detail: A fire damper, smoke damper or manual volume damper upstream of the box has tripped, been left closed or is blocked, starving the box of air while the box damper and controller look normal.

check.name: upstream_damper_inspect
check.text: Locate and inspect the fire/smoke dampers and manual balancing dampers in the supply duct upstream of the box (via access doors) and compare static pressure just before and just after them. Abnormal if a damper blade is closed or partly closed, or the pressure drop across it is more than about 0.1 in. w.c.
